⏳

Coordinate parallel work.

Give independent agents explicit task ownership, dependencies and handoffs. Workstreams can progress without losing track of who is responsible for what.

↔

Keep decisions current.

Tie proposals and approvals to the versions they refer to. When the underlying state changes, an old decision should not silently authorize new work.

↻

Make interruption recoverable.

Preserve completed steps and unresolved actions in checkpoints. Replacement workers should resume from recorded progress and reconcile uncertain outcomes before retrying.

Shared state. Explicit control.

A coordination layer between your agents and their work.

Agents can reason independently. Their actions still need to agree on ownership, dependencies and the state of the workflow. Diya Lamp is being built to make those boundaries explicit.

The open-source Java core will track workstreams, task claims, versioned checkpoints, approval conditions and action records. Agents can connect through language-neutral interfaces; their implementation does not have to be Java.

Start with one workflow you can inspect. Prove that conflicting workers, interrupted handoffs and outdated approvals are handled correctly. Then grow the workload.

Who is Diya Lamp for?

Developers and research teams building multi-agent engineering, analysis and operational workflows. Especially work that spans sessions, involves parallel agents or needs human review before consequential actions.

What does the coordination layer add?

It is intended to keep task ownership, shared context, checkpoints and approvals consistent across independent agents. Durable execution tools can run the steps; Diya Lamp focuses on the coordination rules between them.

What can I use today?

The public Java repository contains earlier persisted review-workflow primitives. General multi-agent coordination is in development. The interactive example is scripted, not a running backend. No months-long workload or regional recovery is claimed as tested.

Where is workflow data stored?

The planned system of record is CockroachDB for all workflow data: tasks, shared context, agent ownership, checkpoints, approvals and execution history. Cross-region replication and configured survival goals support resilience; actual failure tolerance depends on deployment and still needs verification.

Does this guarantee an action happens only once?

No. A database transaction cannot make an arbitrary external API call atomic. Reliable integrations need idempotency where supported and explicit reconciliation when an action’s outcome is uncertain.

Is there a hosted service?

Not yet. The immediate focus is the open-source Java coordination core. Public sign-in, a hosted console and paid service are not available.
